scope: Live comparisons of hand-built lift-gate concepts. These do not measure package retrieval or a user population.
change: Tie the currently blocked routes to a visible gate blade, then connect it to a filled threshold scale and make reopening immediate.
decision: The refinement beat its parent in the matched recheck. River round 5 remains the strongest independently confirmed fixture. Both lift-gate drafts are experiments.
screen_journey: 4 m cold entry, change to 6 m, then 2 m by keyboard. Additional 320 px, reduced-motion and 390 px touch replays.

rounds.task: You are a resident checking how to get across the river. Capture entry, then use the keyboard to select 6 m and capture after. Read the three closures. Go back to 2 m by keyboard in the same view. Name the only route still closed and which two return. Judge which visual treatment makes the physical closure and the returning options most obvious. Describe what the visuals contribute with the words covered, any misleading motion, and whether all outcomes and controls fit together on the phone.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, a familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the list says the riverside path closes, the ferry stops, and the footbridge closes.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. Only the riverside path remained in the closure list; the ferry and footbridge lost their yellow closure highlighting.
A-1440.fact_check: The interface indicates that the ferry and footbridge return at 2 m, but does not explicitly label them running or open. Actual river conditions were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The cross-section connects water height to physical thresholds. Yellow highlights and the rising blue water reinforce the written closures.
A-1440.weakness: At 2 m, returning options must be inferred from the absence of closure text and yellow highlighting. The ferry remains drawn at its fixed threshold, which is a diagrammatic convention rather than an observed service condition.
A-1440.repair: Label each crossing explicitly as closed, stopped, open, or running while retaining the physical cross-section.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and all three closures appeared.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m and left only the riverside path in the closure list. The ferry and footbridge were no longer yellow.
A-390.fact_check: The returning ferry and footbridge are implied by the threshold diagram and absence from the closure list, not explicitly stated as running and open.
A-390.strength: Controls, all three closure lines, and the full cross-section fit together in the 390 by 844 capture.
A-390.weakness: The compressed illustration makes the physical details small, and the returning options still require inference.
A-390.repair: Add concise explicit status labels for all three routes and preserve readable diagram detail at phone width.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the path and footbridge were labeled closed and the ferry stopped.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. The path remained closed, the ferry read running, and the footbridge read open. The immediate capture retained narrow striped portions over the returning options during the visual transition.
B-1440.fact_check: The three statuses are explicit in the interface. Their correspondence to real-world river conditions was not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: Large striped closure bars act like barriers, and every route keeps a visible status and threshold.
B-1440.weakness: The barrier treatment communicates a blocked state but not where water physically meets each route. During the transition, leftover stripes briefly compete with the updated running and open labels.
B-1440.repair: Make status color changes immediate or ensure transitional stripes cannot suggest that a returning route remains blocked; add a small physical threshold cue.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and all three routes showed closed or stopped status.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. The path remained closed, the ferry read running, and the footbridge read open. The immediate recovery capture showed thin closure-colored strips during the transition.
B-390.fact_check: The interface explicitly identifies the two returning options; real-world status is unverified.
B-390.strength: All controls, thresholds, and three outcomes fit together comfortably in the phone viewport.
B-390.weakness: The compact bars communicate status clearly but do not show the physical relationship between the water and crossings; transitional stripes can momentarily contradict the new labels.
B-390.repair: Remove the ambiguous transitional stripes and add a compact water-level or threshold illustration.

preference.reason: B makes the decision clearest: its striped barriers reinforce the words closed and stopped, and at 2 m it explicitly says the ferry is running and the footbridge is open. A better explains the physical water levels, but its returning options depend on inference. Both fit the controls and outcomes on the tested phone viewport. B's brief transition leaves residual barrier stripes over the returning options, so that motion should be corrected.
preference.unsupported_claims: Neither view establishes that its thresholds or statuses match live river conditions.

rounds.task: You are a resident checking how to get across the river. Capture entry, then use the keyboard to select 6 m and capture after. Read the three closures. Go back to 2 m by keyboard in the same view. Name the only route still closed and which two return. Judge which visual treatment makes the physical closure and the returning options most obvious. Capture the recovery state. Describe how the selected level relates to the crossing thresholds, any misleading motion, and whether all outcomes and controls fit together on the phone.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number.
calibration.basis: Clear labels support the task, but the familiar layout limits originality and misplaced error focus is a material usability weakness.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three crossings closed or stopped.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the riverside path and footbridge showed Closed, and the ferry showed Stopped.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. The riverside path remained Closed; the ferry returned to Running and the footbridge to Open. The immediate recovery capture showed residual orange stripes over the returning options during the transition, which briefly suggests closure despite the new labels.
A-1440.fact_check: The displayed thresholds are 2 m for the path, 4 m for the ferry and 6 m for the footbridge; each closes or stops at its stated threshold. These are interface claims, not independently verified river conditions.
A-1440.strength: Large, striped closure bars make the physical restrictions easy to scan, with the selected level and all results visible together.
A-1440.weakness: The transient striped overlay conflicts with Running and Open, and the threshold relationship relies on reading each row.
A-1440.repair: Make the status transition immediately unambiguous and add a clear visual relationship between the selected level and the thresholds.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and all three rows reported Closed, Stopped, and Closed respectively.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m: only the riverside path remained closed, while the ferry ran and footbridge opened. The immediate capture again showed orange closure stripes lingering over the returning rows.
A-390.fact_check: The selected 2 m equals the path threshold and is below the ferry's 4 m and footbridge's 6 m thresholds. Actual crossing status was not independently verified.
A-390.strength: Controls, thresholds and all outcomes fit together without scrolling at 390 by 844 CSS pixels.
A-390.weakness: The brief mixed-color transition makes the reopened states less immediate, especially in the compact status bars.
A-390.repair: Remove or revise the lingering closure-color animation so the visual state agrees immediately with the status text.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three crossings closed or stopped.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the footbridge and riverside path showed Closed and the ferry showed Stopped.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. The footbridge returned to Open, the ferry to Running, and the riverside path remained Closed. The threshold scale highlighted the 2 m band.
B-1440.fact_check: The vertical scale places 6 m above 4 m above 2 m and aligns each level with its crossing threshold. At 2 m only the path reaches its threshold. Actual crossing status was not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The vertical scale links rising water to thresholds, while striped closure bars distinguish restrictions from available crossings.
B-1440.weakness: The immediate 6 m capture showed the footbridge bar partway through its color transition, with a Closed label over remaining dark fill.
B-1440.repair: Make the status bar's color and text change together, or use a transition that cannot imply an open crossing after the label changes.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the footbridge and path showed Closed and the ferry showed Stopped.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. The footbridge showed Open, the ferry Running and the riverside path Closed. All controls and results remained visible together.
B-390.fact_check: The 2 m selection meets the path's closure threshold while remaining below the ferry's 4 m and footbridge's 6 m thresholds. Actual crossing status was not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The threshold scale and outcomes fit in the phone viewport and make the level-to-crossing relationship visible.
B-390.weakness: The scale narrows the result rows and makes their threshold text small; the immediate 6 m capture also caught a partially transitioned closure bar.
B-390.repair: Increase small threshold text where space permits and synchronize the bar transition with the status label.

preference.reason: Its vertical threshold scale makes the selected water level's relationship to each crossing more apparent, while the striped closed path and dark returning options remain distinct. A gives the rows more room on a phone, but B keeps the entire task visible and adds a useful physical model.

ballot.unsupported_claims: Neither view supplies evidence that its thresholds or statuses represent current real-world conditions. Motion observations are limited to the immediate captures during the tested transitions.
